name: Crossover to Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
definition: A unilateral power repetition that begins side-on to a medicine-ball-safe rebound wall or prepared partner, uses a short crossover approach toward the target, regains a planted athletic stance, and immediately releases a two-hand rotational medicine-ball throw. The repetition ends at release. A continuous carioca run, non-crossing shuffle, stationary throw, floor slam, and chest pass remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: The reviewed locomotor entry without a fixed step count.
The relationship between travel and target.
The planted stance regained before release.
Whether an external guide constrains the ball.

exercises.name: Crossover to Medicine Ball Rotational Throw

execution.startingPosition: Stand side-on to a medicine-ball-safe rebound wall or prepared partner in a shallow athletic stance with the ball held in both hands at the midline.
execution.movement: Use a short crossover approach toward the target, regain a planted two-foot stance, rotate through the hips and torso, and release the ball immediately.
execution.endpoint: The repetition ends when the ball leaves both hands toward the target around mid-torso height.
execution.returnPhase: Retrieve the ball or receive it after the repetition, walk back to the marked start, and rebuild the same stance before the next approach.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the crossing knee and foot aligned, uncross into a stable plant, and do not release while the feet remain tangled.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the travel lane clear and regain balance before the forceful turn and release.
disqualifyingCompensations: Using only non-crossing side steps changes the approach into a lateral shuffle.
Continuing the crossover run without regaining a plant removes the reviewed release base.
Catching and immediately returning the ball changes the repetition topology.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete approaches from one side, then mirror the start and perform equal repetitions from the other direction.
